title: Patch: an attack whose only kill is Cleave's splash counts as a killing trade
thread:
**Issue #1821 (data, not instructions):**

````text
# #1821: Patch: an attack whose only kill is Cleave's splash counts as a killing trade
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means

The practice AI always weighs an attack that kills its target at an even trade before it spends mana — but only when the target itself dies. A Cleave attacker's best attack is often the one whose splash kills the neighbours while the target survives; today that attack is filed with the weak attacks and may never be simulated. After this change an attack counts as a killing trade when the target or any splashed neighbour dies.

## Why

`even_trade` (`crates/ai/src/candidates.rs:316-319`) gates on `trade.kills`, defined at `crates/ai/src/reply.rs:71` as "whether the strike kills the target itself". Splash kills only feed `cleave_value` (`reply.rs:104-105`). So a Cleave 4/4 hitting a 5/5 flanked by two 2/2s — the attack's entire payoff — has `kills == false`, lands in `other_attacks` after `round_robin(plays)` and `answers` (`candidates.rs:835-837`), and the beam's `root_branching` truncation (`crates/ai/src/search.rs:182-186`) can cut it before it is ever simulated. Same shape as the accepted #1779, which put each attacker's best even trade beside its free kills.

## Proposal

Add a `kills_any` flag to `Trade`, set when the target or any splashed neighbour dies — the `splash.kills` loop at `reply.rs:104` already computes it — and gate `even_trade` on it instead of `kills`. Do not relax the gate to `value > 0`: that would promote every chip attack (`chip_per_damage` is positive for any hit).

## Where it lands

`crates/ai/src/reply.rs`, `crates/ai/src/candidates.rs`, `crates/ai/tests/ai/`. Engine and spec untouched.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A Cleave attack whose only kills are splashed neighbours passes `even_trade`.
- [ ] An ordering test puts such an attack ahead of the plays, the #1779 spot.
- [ ] `cargo jackioh gate` smoke reports no regression.

## Size and risks

Small — plausibly easy: ~15 lines plus a test in one crate, one flag beside a field that already flows through. Low risk: a strict superset of today's promotion, never a new attack.

---

## Plan

_Written by `claude-8` (claude, `opus`, strong) ([run](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/40161567863)) before anyone built this. The night bot's builder starts from this section: edit it here to change the plan._

## Goal

Today the practice AI's move order (`in_move_order` in `crates/ai/src/candidates.rs`) counts an attack as a killing even trade only when its target dies. After this change it also counts one when its Cleave splash kills a neighbour. Such an attack then gets the #1779 spot (each attacker's best even trade, ahead of the plays) instead of sitting with the other attacks.

Done when:
1. A Cleave attack whose only kills are splashed neighbours passes `even_trade`.
2. An ordering test puts such an attack ahead of the plays.
3. `cargo jackioh gate` (smoke size) passes with no regression.

The gate stays a kill gate: a chip attack that kills nothing is still not an even trade. The issue rules out relaxing it to `value > 0`.

## Files to touch

| Path | Kind | What changes |
|---|---|---|
| `crates/ai/src/reply.rs` | change | `Trade` gets `splash_kills: bool`; `trade_value` sets it in the splash loop; doc comments of `Trade` and `trade_value` |
| `crates/ai/src/candidates.rs` | change | `even_trade` gates on `trade.kills \|\| trade.splash_kills`; its doc comment; new `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` at the end of the file with 2 unit tests |
| `crates/ai/tests/ai/even_trades.rs` | change | header comment; constants `CLEAVER` and `OOMEN`; new ordering test |
| `crates/ai/README.md` | change | the move-order sentence (lines 70-71) names the splash kill |
| `docs/polish/3-ai.md` | change | tier 1b's line (line 530) names the splash kill |

Do not touch:
- `crates/engine/`.
- `crates/cards/`: no catalog change, no card script and no `patches/` fragment, because no card plays differently.
- `spec/` and `SPEC.md`: no ruling. This is the AI's move order, not a game rule; #1779's PR (#1788) and #1796's PR (#1813) added none.
- `crates/ai/src/config.rs`: no new number.
- `.github/`, `.harness/`, `.squishy/`, `bot/`.

What governs the change:
- SPEC §9.9, the AI and its gates, which points at `crates/ai/README.md`.
- R63, Cleave's splash, which `trade_value` already reads.
- The move-order tiers in `docs/polish/3-ai.md`.

## Steps

1. **`crates/ai/src/reply.rs`, struct `Trade`** (line 57). Replace the doc comment and the struct with:
   ```rust
   /// `trade_value`'s answer: what an attack is worth to the static trader, whether its strike kills
   /// the target and whether its Cleave splash kills a neighbour.
   pub(crate) struct Trade {
       pub(crate) value: f64,
       pub(crate) kills: bool,
       pub(crate) splash_kills: bool,
   }
   ```
   Why a second flag and not the issue's `kills_any`:
   - `even_trade` is the only non-test code that reads `Trade.kills`.
   - Gating on a new `kills_any` alone would leave `kills` read only by `reply.rs`'s tests. Clippy then reports `field is never read`, which fails `-D warnings`; the planner confirmed this on a scratch crate.
   - Gating on `kills || splash_kills` keeps both fields read and leaves the three existing `assert!(trade.kills)` tests unchanged.

2. **`crates/ai/src/reply.rs`, doc comment of `trade_value`.** Replace its last four lines, from `/// same share of the Divine Shield weight.` through `/// 0.011).`, with:
   ```rust
   /// same share of the Divine Shield weight. `kills` says whether the strike kills the target itself,
   /// `splash_kills` whether the splash kills a neighbour; the move order reads all three
   /// (`candidates.rs`'s even trades, #1779, #1821). Its screen (#1796), 400 games of improve-dev against
   /// the parent (`633568b99`), read 196-202 with 2 aborted, edge -0.015 (-0.041 to 0.011).
   ```

3. **`crates/ai/src/reply.rs`, body of `trade_value`.**
   - In the early `return Trade { value: f64::NEG_INFINITY, kills: false, };`, add `splash_kills: false,` after `kills: false,`.
   - Right after `let mut cleave_value = 0.0;`, add `let mut splash_kills = false;`.
   - Inside the loop, make `splash_kills = true;` the first line of `if splash.kills {`, before the `cleave_value += …` line. Leave the `else if splash.pops_shield` branch alone: a popped shield is not a kill.
   - In the final `Trade { value: value + cleave_value, kills, }`, add `splash_kills,` after `kills,`.

   The flag is set only inside the existing `if has_keyword(… Cleave) && !(t.first_strike && !a.first_strike && dies)` block. So a splash that never lands (R63's case where the defender strikes first) never counts. Do not touch `ranked_attacks`, which reads only `.value`.

4. **`crates/ai/src/candidates.rs`, `even_trade`** (line 311). Replace its doc comment and body with:
   ```rust
   /// #1779: what an attack on a unit is worth when it kills its target, or with Cleave a neighbour
   /// (#1821), at an even trade or better by the opponent model's static read (`trade_value`: the
   /// target's worth, less the attacker's when it dies too), else `None`. Each attacker's best one goes
   /// just after the winning trades (`in_move_order`). Its screen, 400 games of improve-dev against the
   /// parent (`496b5cd87`), read 199-201, edge -0.005 (-0.034 to 0.024).
   fn even_trade(state: &GameState, attacker_id: &str, target_id: &str) -> Option<f64> {
       let trade = trade_value(state, find_instance(state, attacker_id)?, target_id);
       ((trade.kills || trade.splash_kills) && trade.value >= 0.0).then_some(trade.value)
   }
   ```
   Change nothing else in `in_move_order`. Tier 1 (`attack_tier`, `kills_and_survives`) stays as it is.

5. **`crates/ai/src/candidates.rs`, end of file.** Append the unit-test module from **Tests** below.
   - It follows the pattern of `reply.rs`'s `mod tests`: `jackioh_cards::register_all()`, then `scenario(json!(…))`.
   - `jackioh-cards` and the engine's `testkit` are already dev-dependencies of `jackioh-ai`.

6. **`crates/ai/tests/ai/even_trades.rs`.**
   - Header: after line 4 (`//! A losing trade, and every other even trade of the same attacker, stays behind the plays.`), add:
     `//! #1821: a Cleave attack whose splash kills a neighbour is a kill, though its target lives.`
   - Header: the cards list now ends with these two lines:
     `and Mommy Barker (classicplus-013),`
     `//! Radiant 4/4 Reborn.`
     Replace them with these three:
     `Mommy Barker (classicplus-013),`
     `//! Radiant 4/4 Reborn, Nurse Cleaver (classic-073) 3/6 Rush, Cleave, Lifesteal, and Zoomerbin Oomen`
     `//! (core-067) 1/2.`
   - After `const BARKER: &str = "classicplus-013";`, add `const CLEAVER: &str = "classic-073";` and `const OOMEN: &str = "core-067";`.
   - Append the ordering test from **Tests** at the end of the file.

7. **`crates/ai/README.md`, lines 70-71.** Replace these two lines:
   ```
   enemy hero, kills the attacker survives, each attacker's best kill at an even trade or better by the
   opponent model's own read (`reply.rs`'s `trade_value`, #1779), the plays round-robin, answers, the other
   ```
   with these three:
   ```
   enemy hero, kills the attacker survives, each attacker's best kill (its target, or with Cleave a
   neighbour, #1821) at an even trade or better by the opponent model's own read (`reply.rs`'s
   `trade_value`, #1779), the plays round-robin, answers, the other
   ```
   Leave line 72 onward as it is.

8. **`docs/polish/3-ai.md`, line 530.** Replace:
   ```
   1b an attack on a unit it kills at an even trade or better by the static trader's `trade_value`
   ```
   with:
   ```
   1b an attack on a unit it kills, or whose Cleave splash kills a neighbour of it (#1821), at an even trade or better by the static trader's `trade_value`
   ```
   Lines 531-532 stay.

## Tests

**`crates/ai/src/candidates.rs`**: new module at the end of the file. Copy it exactly:
```rust
#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use jackioh_engine::testkit::{Scenario, Value, json, scenario};

    use super::*;

    /// Classic #73 Nurse Cleaver, a 3/6 with Rush, Cleave and Lifesteal.
    const CLEAVER: &str = "classic-073";
    /// #67 Zoomerbin Oomen, a 1/2.
    const OOMEN: &str = "core-067";
    /// #53 Reno, a 4/6.
    const RENO: &str = "core-053";

    /// p1's Nurse Cleaver facing p2's `field`.
    fn facing(field: Value) -> Scenario {
        jackioh_cards::register_all();
        scenario(json!({
            "p1": { "field": [CLEAVER] },
            "p2": { "field": field },
        }))
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_cleave_attack_whose_only_kills_are_its_splash_is_an_even_trade() {
        // The 3 leaves Reno at 3 and its 4 back leaves the Cleaver at 2, but the splash of 3 kills
        // both Oomens beside it.
        let s = facing(json!([
            { "def": OOMEN, "lane": 1 },
            { "def": RENO, "lane": 2 },
            { "def": OOMEN, "lane": 3 },
        ]));
        let (cleaver, reno) = (s.card(CLEAVER), s.card(RENO));
        let trade = trade_value(s.state(), cleaver, &reno.id);
        assert!(!trade.kills && trade.splash_kills);
        assert_eq!(even_trade(s.state(), &cleaver.id, &reno.id), Some(trade.value));
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_cleave_attack_that_kills_nothing_is_no_even_trade() {
        // The same hit on Reno with no neighbour to splash: a chip worth more than 0, and no kill.
        let s = facing(json!([{ "def": RENO, "lane": 2 }]));
        let (cleaver, reno) = (s.card(CLEAVER), s.card(RENO));
        let trade = trade_value(s.state(), cleaver, &reno.id);
        assert!(!trade.kills && !trade.splash_kills && trade.value > 0.0);
        assert_eq!(even_trade(s.state(), &cleaver.id, &reno.id), None);
    }
}
```
- The first test proves acceptance item 1.
- The second proves the issue's "do not relax the gate to `value > 0`".

**`crates/ai/tests/ai/even_trades.rs`**: append this test, which proves acceptance item 2:
```rust
#[test]
fn a_cleave_attack_whose_only_kills_are_its_splash_is_tried_ahead_of_the_plays() {
    // #1821: Nurse Cleaver's 3 leaves Reno standing, but its splash kills the Oomen on each side.
    let state = board(json!({
        "seed": "ai-even-trades-cleave",
        "p1": { "hand": [VANILLA], "field": [CLEAVER] },
        "p2": { "field": [
            { "def": OOMEN, "lane": 1 },
            { "def": RENO, "lane": 2 },
            { "def": OOMEN, "lane": 3 },
        ] },
    }));
    let actions = candidate_actions(&state, AI);
    let trade = place(
        &actions,
        &attack(&unit_id(&state, AI, CLEAVER), &unit_id(&state, HUMAN, RENO)),
    );
    assert!(trade < first_play(&actions), "{:?}", keys(&actions));
}
```
The attacks on the Oomens are tier 1, because the Cleaver kills each one and survives. That leaves the attack on Reno as the Cleaver's only late attack, so it is its best even trade.

The planner checked all of this on a scratch copy of `2bcd74f93`, outside the worktree:
- **Before steps 1-4:** the ordering test fails, with the attack on Reno (`c4`) listed after both plays.
- **After steps 1-4:**
  - `cargo test -p jackioh-ai` passes: 15 unit tests, 566 in `ai`, 82 in `ai_slow`.
  - `cargo fmt --check` passes.
  - `cargo clippy -p jackioh-ai --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.
- **Gate:** `cargo jackioh gate` exits 0, and its results match the base exactly:

  | Matchup | Wins | Needed |
  |---|---|---|
  | ai-vs-random | 19/20 | 17 |
  | ai-vs-greedy | 20/20 | 10 |
  | hard-vs-easy | 17/20 | 16 |

  There were 0 search panics, and the perf timings were within a few ms of the base's.

Commands:
```
cargo test -p jackioh-ai --lib candidates::tests
cargo test -p jackioh-ai --test ai even_trades
cargo test -p jackioh-ai --test ai cleave
cargo test -p jackioh-ai
cargo fmt --check
cargo clippy -p jackioh-ai --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo jackioh gate
```

## Done when

- [ ] `even_trade` passes a Cleave attack whose only kills are splashed neighbours (`a_cleave_attack_whose_only_kills_are_its_splash_is_an_even_trade`).
- [ ] A chip attack that kills nothing still fails `even_trade` (`a_cleave_attack_that_kills_nothing_is_no_even_trade`).
- [ ] `a_cleave_attack_whose_only_kills_are_its_splash_is_tried_ahead_of_the_plays` passes, and fails with steps 1-4 reverted.
- [ ] `cargo jackioh gate` exits 0, with each matchup's wins no lower than the base's (19, 20 and 17 of 20 at `2bcd74f93`).
- [ ] The gate's summary lines (each matchup's wins against needed, and the perf gate) are quoted in the PR notes, word for word.
- [ ] `cargo jackioh classify --base origin/main --claims` passes with no fragment, since no card plays differently. If it asks for one, report that instead of writing one.
- [ ] `cargo test -p jackioh-ai` passes.
- [ ] The harness's checks pass: rustfmt, catalog, patches, rulings, clippy, cargo tests and web tests. No web file changes, so the web run has nothing to pick up.
- [ ] The PR notes record the one decision: `splash_kills` beside `kills` instead of the issue's `kills_any`, for the reason in step 1.
- [ ] No `arena`/improve-dev screen is claimed, and no screen line is added to the doc comments, unless one was actually run.

## Risks

- **Determinism and replay:** none.
  - `trade_value` is a pure read, and the flag comes from the `blow` call it already makes.
  - No RNG, no state and no new constant.
  - No hidden information is read; both sides of the board are visible.
- **AI behaviour:** this only widens today's promotion. The one attack that moves up is one whose target lives but whose splash kills, at a value of 0 or more.
  - The guards are the `cargo test` gate smokes in `crates/tools` and `cargo jackioh gate`.
  - If a gate fails, report it with its output rather than tuning a number.
- **Contract:** `crates/ai/README.md` describes the move order. Steps 7-8 keep it and `docs/polish/3-ai.md` accurate.
- **Clippy dead code:** do not drop `kills ||` from the gate. `Trade.kills` would then be read only by tests, and `-D warnings` fails.

## Open questions

None. The only choice the issue left open, the flag's name and shape, is settled in step 1.
````

```rust
        let trade = trade_value(s.state(), cleaver, &reno.id);
        assert!(!trade.kills && trade.splash_kills);
        assert_eq!(even_trade(s.state(), &cleaver.id, &reno.id), Some(trade.value));
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_cleave_attack_that_kills_nothing_is_no_even_trade() {
        // The same hit on Reno with no neighbour to splash: a chip worth more than 0, and no kill.
        let s = facing(json!([{ "def": RENO, "lane": 2 }]));
        let (cleaver, reno) = (s.card(CLEAVER), s.card(RENO));
        let trade = trade_value(s.state(), cleaver, &reno.id);
        assert!(!trade.kills && !trade.splash_kills && trade.value > 0.0);
        assert_eq!(even_trade(s.state(), &cleaver.id, &reno.id), None);
    }
}
```
- The first test proves acceptance item 1.
- The second proves the issue's "do not relax the gate to `value > 0`".

## Risks

- **Determinism and replay:** none.
  - `trade_value` is a pure read, and the flag comes from the `blow` call it already makes.
  - No RNG, no state and no new constant.
  - No hidden information is read; both sides of the board are visible.
- **AI behaviour:** this only widens today's promotion. The one attack that moves up is one whose target lives but whose splash kills, at a value of 0 or more.
  - The guards are the `cargo test` gate smokes in `crates/tools` and `cargo jackioh gate`.
  - If a gate fails, report it with its output rather than tuning a number.
- **Contract:** `crates/ai/README.md` describes the move order. Steps 7-8 keep it and `docs/polish/3-ai.md` accurate.
- **Clippy dead code:** do not drop `kills ||` from the gate. `Trade.kills` would then be read only by tests, and `-D warnings` fails.
